title: Topic 75 | Image formation in plane and spherical mirrors

questions.text: If the angle between the reflected ray and a plane mirror is $22^\circ$, what is the angle of incidence?
If the angle between the surface of a horizontal plane mirror and the ray incident on it is $20^\circ$, what is the angle of reflection (in degrees)?
The angle between a mirror and the incident ray is $35^\circ$. Determine the angle of reflection of the light.
If the angle between the ray incident on a plane mirror and the ray reflected from it is $20^\circ$, what is the angle of incidence of the ray?
If the mirror is rotated through $15^\circ$, through how many degrees does the ray reflected from the mirror turn?
If a plane mirror is rotated through an angle $\alpha=28^\circ$, through what angle does the reflected ray turn?
As a result of rotating a plane mirror, the ray reflected from it deviated from its original direction by an angle $\alpha$. Through what angle was the mirror rotated?

A light ray is incident on a plane mirror at an angle of $22^\circ$. If the mirror is rotated (the incident ray is unchanged) so that the angle of incidence becomes $36^\circ$, through what angle has the reflected ray turned?
The altitude of the Sun above the horizon is $46^\circ$. What must the angle of incidence of the sunlight on a plane mirror be for the reflected ray to go vertically upward?
Sunlight makes an angle of $40^\circ$ with the ground. At what angle to the horizontal should a plane mirror be placed to direct the ray into a thin tube set perpendicular to the ground?

Two plane mirrors make an angle of $60^\circ$ with each other. What must the angle of incidence of a ray on the first mirror be so that the ray reflected from the first mirror strikes the surface of the second mirror perpendicularly?
What is the angle $\alpha$ between the mirrors (in degrees)?
A light ray is incident on one of two mirrors placed at an angle of $20^\circ$ to each other. What is the angle between the ray reflected from both mirrors and the incident ray?
A mirror is immersed in water at an angle. If $\alpha=20^\circ$, find the angles $\beta$ and $\gamma$.
Find the angle of reflection of the ray from mirror $L$.
If $I$ is the ray incident on a plane mirror and $I'$ is the reflected ray, find the angle $\alpha$.
Sunlight makes an angle of $36^\circ$ with the ground. What must the angle of incidence on the mirror be so that the ray, after reflection from a plane mirror, travels horizontally?
At what angle $\alpha$ to the ground must a plane mirror be placed so that the ray, after reflection from it, travels horizontally?
A light ray is incident on one of two mirrors placed at an angle of $30^\circ$ to each other. What is the angle between the ray reflected from both mirrors and the incident ray?
The figure shows the path of a ray that strikes mirrors placed at an angle $\alpha$ to each other and is reflected from them. Through what total angle is the ray deviated from its original direction?
If the image of an object in a plane mirror is formed at a distance of $70$ cm from the mirror, what is the distance between the object and its image (in cm)?
A person stands in front of a plane mirror. How does the distance between the person and the image change if the person moves $1$ m closer to the mirror?
If a boy moves $4$ m closer to the plane of a vertical mirror, by how many meters does his image in the mirror move closer to him?
If a person's distance of best vision is $30$ cm, at what distance from the mirror (in cm) should the person stand to see his own image better?
How does the distance between a person and the image change if the person moves $2.6$ m closer to the plane of a vertical plane mirror?
How does the distance between a person and the image change if the person moves $3$ m farther from the plane of a vertical plane mirror?
A boy sees his reflection in a plane mirror. If he approaches the mirror at a speed of $0.6$ m/s, at what speed (in m/s) does his reflection approach him?

A plane mirror moves perpendicular to its plane toward a light source at a speed of $1.5$ cm/s. At what speed (in cm/s) and in which direction must the light source move so that its image in the mirror remains stationary?
A girl approaches a mirror perpendicular to it at a speed of $0.5$ m/s. At what speeds (in m/s) does the girl's image approach her and the mirror, respectively?

Mirror OA rotates with angular velocity $\omega$ about an axis perpendicular to the plane of the drawing and passing through point O. If $OS=l$, at what speed does the image of point S move at the moment shown in the figure?
Point A moves horizontally at a speed $v_1=3$ m/s, and plane mirror MN moves vertically at a speed $v_2=4$ m/s, as shown in the figure. Find the speed of the image of point A in the mirror (in m/s).
Point A moves horizontally at a speed $v_1=8$ m/s, and plane mirror MN moves vertically at a speed $v_2=3$ m/s, as shown in the figure. Find the speed of the image of point A in the mirror (in m/s).
What is the minimum height (in m) of a vertical plane mirror in which a girl $1.6$ m tall, without changing the position of her head, can see her whole image?
answers: the answer depends on the distance between the girl and the mirror.
